context_requirements: Expression of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) and a catecholamine-synthesizing phenotype
Presence of intracellular dopamine pools whose loss can be sensed transcriptionally
None of the nine landmark-profiled lines are known to be catecholaminergic
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in landmark gene expression at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine lines
Shared transcriptional signature across lines that is absent in vehicle controls
Evidence of dopamine-responsive gene expression changes (e.g., TH, DDC, DBH, SLC6A3, SLC18A2) in these lines

evidence.supports: alpha-methyl-p-tyrosine, a tyrosine hydroxylase inhibitor, reduced dopamine-dependent caspase-3 activation in dopaminergic PC-12 cells, indicating TH inhibition can modulate apoptosis only in catecholamine-producing cells
alpha-methyl-p-tyrosine blocked endogenous dopamine production in mouse lymphocytes, showing TH inhibition affects cells with catecholamine synthesis capacity

changes: Removed PMID 12899705: the abstract describes 3-iodotyrosine only as an injected agent altering dopamine-related neurotoxicity in insect larvae and does not establish it as a tyrosine hydroxylase inhibitor supporting the stated claim.
No gene-level direction, specificity, line-response, kinetics, or magnitude corrections were required because all gene lists and effect fields were empty/none.
